summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

key_cases.case_name: In Re the Appeal in Cochise County Juvenile Action No. 5666-J
key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court vacated the court of appeals' opinion and affirmed the juvenile court's dismissal of the dependency petition, holding that Santosky's clear-and-convincing standard is confined to termination and that dependency must be proved only by a preponderance of the evidence, which the State had not done.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Arizona authority on the dependency burden of proof, which the later court of appeals decisions merely follow and expressly cite.
key_cases.quote: the weighing of the private and public interests convinces us that the preponderance of the evidence standard is the proper standard of proof in dependency proceedings

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed and remanded, holding that an unwed father was denied due process and equal protection when Illinois declared his children dependent and removed them on a presumption of unfitness without any hearing on his actual fitness as a parent.
key_cases.relevance: A majority-opinion source for the parental liberty interest at the moment the State files to take a child, supplying the authority this brief correctly declined to draw from the Troxel plurality.
key_cases.quote: We have concluded that all Illinois parents are constitutionally entitled to a hearing on their fitness before their children are removed from their custody

key_cases.case_name: Louis C. v. Department of Child Safety
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed the dependency adjudication, holding that A.R.S. § 8-844(C) requires the juvenile court to adjudicate dependency on a preponderance of the evidence and that the Parents' Bill of Rights does not raise that burden.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Arizona statement of the burden of proof at dependency adjudication.
key_cases.quote: Section 8-844(C) not only permits a court to enter an order of dependency based on a preponderance of the evidence, but directs that a court "shall" do so.

key_cases.case_name: Oscar F. v. Department of Child Safety
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed the dependency adjudication, holding the juvenile court had statutory authority to find the children dependent as to one parent notwithstanding the petition's allegations or the failure to serve the other parent or guardian.
key_cases.relevance: Governs the pleading and service defects that do not defeat a dependency petition.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court was authorized by statute to adjudicate the children dependent as to Oscar, notwithstanding allegations in the petition or that another parent or guardian has not been served.

key_cases.case_name: Dep't of Child Safety v. Stocking-Tate
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals granted special action relief and vacated the order striking the ex parte temporary custody order, holding that an ex parte removal order is not challenged by a motion to strike but is reviewed at the statutory temporary custody hearing, where DCS bears the probable-cause burden.
key_cases.relevance: Explains that the ex parte order expires unless a dependency petition is filed within 72 hours.
key_cases.quote: DCS bears the burden of proving "there is probable cause to believe that continued temporary custody of the child is clearly necessary to prevent abuse or neglect."

key_cases.case_name: In re Termination of Parental Rights as to M.N.
key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court reversed and remanded, holding that a man identified as a potential father and served with notice under A.R.S. § 8-106(G) is not required to file with the putative fathers registry and so cannot have his rights terminated under § 8-533(B)(6) for failing to do so.
key_cases.relevance: Governs who must be served and what notice-based grounds may be pleaded when the agency or a private party opens a case affecting an alleged father's rights.
key_cases.quote: a potential father's rights cannot be terminated under § 8-533(B)(6) for noncompliance with § 8-106.01
